does: Cooks a flat piece of food in a thin layer of hot fat, turning it once.
how: Heat a film of fat in the pan over medium heat.
Lay the food in, away from you, and leave it alone.
Turn it once, when the underside is golden and it lifts without sticking.
For an egg, keep the heat gentle and spoon hot fat over the white until it is set.

cues.text: A steady, gentle sizzle. Spitting means the heat is too high or the food is wet.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the food again and again, so that it never browns.
mistakes.fix: Turn it once. If it sticks, it is not ready to turn.

variant_of.differs: Larger, flat pieces that lie still and are turned once, over gentler heat.
